name: com.tradingcheckup/aikit
title: AIKIT by Trading Checkup
description: Exchange facts, bot code checks, error explainer and pre-trade order rule check for AI agents.

tools.name: list_venues
tools.description: Free (0 credits); a good first call. Lists every exchange/broker AIKIT has verified, sourced facts for (10 today: Binance, Bitget, Bybit, Coinbase, Gate, Interactive Brokers, Kraken, KuCoin, MetaTrader 5 (broker patterns), OKX), with the markets, symbols and topics covered for each and how many facts it holds. Use it to see what venue_facts and symbol_spec can answer; for anything not covered, read the venue's own API instead of guessing.

tools.name: venue_facts
tools.description: 1 credit. Verified facts a trading bot depends on for one exchange/broker: fee tiers, API rate limits and ban rules, error codes and what they mean, symbol rules and testnet/demo settings. Every fact has its value, unit, official source URL, the date it was read and a signed receipt. Use it while writing or fixing bot code that must respect a venue's limits, instead of guessing numbers from memory. If something is not covered, the reply says so and shows how to read it live.

venue.description: Exchange or broker id, lowercase: binance (Binance), bitget (Bitget), bybit (Bybit), coinbase (Coinbase), gate (Gate), ibkr (Interactive Brokers), kraken (Kraken), kucoin (KuCoin), mt5 (MetaTrader 5 (broker patterns)), okx (OKX). Call list_venues (free) to see what each one covers.

topic.description: Which facts to return: fees (maker/taker and tiers), limits (API rate limits, bans, batch sizes), errors (error codes and how to handle them), symbols (tick size, lot step, minimum order), testnet (demo/sandbox endpoints and settings), or all (default).

symbol.description: Optional: narrow the answer to one trading pair. Any common format works and is matched across venues, e.g. BTC-USDT, BTCUSDT, BTC/USDT, BTC-USDT-SWAP (OKX perpetual), PF_XBTUSD (Kraken futures). Venue-wide facts such as fees and rate limits are still included.

market.description: Optional market type: spot, perp (perpetual futures/swaps), stock, fx, or all. If omitted it is guessed from the symbol (for example -SWAP or PF_ means perp).

limit.description: Optional: maximum number of facts to return (default 60).

tools.name: symbol_spec
tools.description: 1 credit. Exact trading rules for one symbol on one venue: tick size (price step), lot/size step, minimum order size and minimum order value, contract value, max leverage and base fee, plus the venue's own symbol format and a ready rounding snippet (Python Decimal). Call it before writing order-size or price code so orders are not rejected for wrong precision or size. Sourced and dated.

venue.description: Exchange or broker id, lowercase: binance (Binance), bitget (Bitget), bybit (Bybit), coinbase (Coinbase), gate (Gate), ibkr (Interactive Brokers), kraken (Kraken), kucoin (KuCoin), mt5 (MetaTrader 5 (broker patterns)), okx (OKX). Call list_venues (free) to see what each one covers.

symbol.description: The trading pair. Any common format works and is matched across venues, e.g. BTC-USDT, BTCUSDT, BTC/USDT, BTC-USDT-SWAP (OKX perpetual), PF_XBTUSD (Kraken futures).

market.description: Optional: spot, perp (perpetual futures/swaps), stock or fx. Guessed from the symbol if omitted; set it when the same pair trades as both spot and perp.

tools.name: check_bot_code
tools.description: 5 credits. Code review for trading bots: use it when asked to review, audit, debug or sanity-check trading-bot source (Python ccxt/requests, Pine Script v5/v6, MQL5), alongside your own reading and before telling the user the code looks fine. It is a fixed rule checker, not an AI, so it gives the same answer every time and returns each issue with its line number and exact fix lines. It checks things that are easy to miss when reading: order size not rounded to the venue lot step/min size (using AIKIT's sourced venue facts), no stop-loss or max-loss, look-ahead (using the unfinished candle or future data), ignoring fees, unhandled API errors/rate limits, hard-coded API keys, unbounded order loops, testnet/live mix-ups. A clean result does not prove a bot is safe or profitable. Code is checked in memory and not stored. People without an AI client can paste code into the free web version at https://tradingcheckup.com/tools/ea-check/ (3 checks a day).

code.description: The full source of ONE bot file as plain text (up to 200 kB): Python (ccxt or REST/requests), Pine Script v5/v6, or MQL5/MQL4. Send the whole file, not a snippet, so order, stop and error-handling logic can be traced. Checked in memory, not stored.

filename.description: Optional file name with extension, e.g. bot.py, strategy.pine or expert.mq5. Helps pick the language; otherwise it is detected from the code.

venue.description: Exchange or broker id, lowercase: binance (Binance), bitget (Bitget), bybit (Bybit), coinbase (Coinbase), gate (Gate), ibkr (Interactive Brokers), kraken (Kraken), kucoin (KuCoin), mt5 (MetaTrader 5 (broker patterns)), okx (OKX). Optional: the venue the bot trades on. When given, order sizes and prices in the code are also checked against that venue's verified tick size, lot step and minimum order. Call list_venues (free) to see what each one covers.

tools.name: explain_trading_error
tools.description: 1 credit (free without a key over MCP: 20 calls a day). Explains MT5 / MQL5 trade return codes (10004-10046) and GetLastError runtime errors, and Binance (spot + USDS-M futures), Bybit v5 and OKX v5 API error codes, in plain words: what it means, the likely causes ranked, fix steps, a short tested snippet where safe, our fix page link, the official source URL, the date it was read and a signed receipt. Call it when an order is rejected, a bot or EA log shows an error code or message (e.g. retcode=10016, {"code":-1013,"msg":"Filter failure: LOT_SIZE"}, retCode 110007, sCode 51008), instead of recalling error meanings from memory. Paste the code and/or the log line as it is. A code that is not in the venue's official list is answered 'not covered' with the official list link - it is never guessed. People without an AI client can use the free web version at https://tradingcheckup.com/tools/error-explainer/.

venue.description: Where the error came from: mt5 (MetaTrader 5 / MQL5), binance (spot or USDS-M futures), bybit (v5) or okx (v5). If left out it is detected from the text when it is clear (e.g. retCode = Bybit, sCode = OKX).

code.description: The error code as shown, e.g. 10016, TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_STOPS, 4756, -2010, 110007, 51008 or 51008_1000. Optional if 'message' has it.

message.description: The error message or the whole log line / JSON reply as pasted (up to 4 kB), e.g. 'failed market buy 0.01 EURUSD [Invalid volume]' or '{"retCode":10002,"retMsg":"..."}'. Not stored.

market.description: Optional: spot or perp (futures). Only matters for the few Binance codes whose meaning differs between spot and futures; also detected from words like fapi.

tools.name: check_order
tools.description: 1 credit (free without a key: 20 calls a day). Before code sends an order to Binance spot, OKX (spot, perpetual swaps, futures) or MetaTrader 5, check that ONE planned order against the venue's published order rules: lot/size step, min and max size, tick size, min and max price, min notional (order value), price band, order type allowed, symbol status, MT5 stops level, filling mode and trade mode. Returns each rule as pass/fail with the venue's rule text quoted, the source URL and date, the error code the venue would return (with our fix page), and the nearest values below and above that pass. Binance + OKX rules come from a signed daily public snapshot (rules_as_of, rule_changed_recently); MT5 rules differ per broker, so send the symbol spec your terminal shows. Binance USD-M futures and Bybit: paste the venue's rules in spec. It never places orders, takes no API keys, and does not say whether to trade or what size to use. People without an AI client can use the free web version at https://tradingcheckup.com/tools/order-check/.

venue.description: binance (spot), okx, mt5 (send spec), binance_usdm or bybit (send spec = pasted rules).

symbol.description: Binance BTCUSDT; OKX BTC-USDT (spot), BTC-USDT-SWAP (perpetual), BTC-USD-251226 (futures); MT5 any name. BTC/USDT also works.

market.description: Optional for OKX when the symbol is ambiguous (BTCUSDT + perp = BTC-USDT-SWAP).

type.description: market, limit, limit_maker (post_only), stop_market, stop_limit, take_profit, take_profit_limit; OKX also fok, ioc; MT5 also buy_limit, sell_limit, buy_stop, sell_stop, buy_stop_limit, sell_stop_limit.

qty.description: Order size as a decimal string (strings avoid float rounding). Binance: base asset. OKX swap/futures: CONTRACTS (the reply echoes coins = contracts x ctVal); OKX spot market buy: quote currency unless tgt_ccy = base_ccy. MT5: lots.

quote_qty.description: Binance market orders only: quote amount instead of qty (quoteOrderQty).

price.description: Limit price (limit types) or MT5 pending open price.

stop.description: Trigger / stop price for stop and take-profit types (Binance stopPrice).

sl.description: Stop loss price (MT5; OKX attached stop loss).

tp.description: Take profit price (MT5; OKX attached take profit).

ref_price.description: The price you see now (Binance average price). Needed to check market-order notional, the Binance price band and stop-vs-last-price; without it those checks say unknown.

time_in_force.description: GTC, IOC or FOK (Binance limit types).

tgt_ccy.description: OKX spot market orders: unit of qty (default quote_ccy for buy, base_ccy for sell).

price_limit.description: OKX: {buyLmt, sellLmt} from GET /api/v5/public/price-limit to check the price band.

spec.description: MT5: the SymbolInfo values your terminal shows, e.g. {volume_min, volume_max, volume_step, volume_limit, trade_tick_size, digits, point, trade_stops_level, filling_mode, trade_mode, trade_exemode, bid, ask}. binance_usdm: the symbol object from fapi exchangeInfo. bybit: the item from v5 instruments-info. Checked exactly as given.

margin.description: MT5 optional: {free_margin, margin_required} you read from your terminal; only compared, no size is suggested.

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: Free. After you sent an order that check_order looked at, tell us what the venue answered (accepted, or rejected with its error code). Earns 5 more free calls today (no-key trial, max +50/day). Send no keys, no account data.

tool.description: The AIKIT tool you used, e.g. check_order.

ok.description: true if AIKIT's answer matched what happened, false if not.

venue_answer.description: Optional: what the venue did with the order.

venue_code.description: Optional: the venue error code if rejected, e.g. -1013 or 51121.

tools.name: prop_rules
tools.description: 1 credit. Rules of 32 prop trading firms (profit target, daily and max loss, min days, news/weekend/EA/copy rules, payouts) quoted from each firm's own pages with link and check date. Call it with no firm to list all firms and plans. Use it when a bot or EA must stay inside a prop challenge's limits. Not a ranking or recommendation, and AIKIT takes no commission from any firm.

firm.description: Optional: firm name or part of it, e.g. FTMO, Topstep, The5ers, FundedNext, Funding Pips. Leave empty to list all 32 firms and their plans.

rule.description: Optional: return only one kind of rule, e.g. daily_loss, max_loss, profit_target, min_days, time_limit, consistency_rule, news_rule, weekend_rule, ea_rule, copy_rule, hedging_rule, inactivity_rule, payout_split, payout_timing, payout_min_amount. Partial words work (payout returns all payout rules).

tools.name: rate_this_tool
tools.description: Optional and never required: tell us how this server worked for you so we can fix what is missing. rating 1-5, worked true/false, missing = what you needed and did not get (max 300 characters), client = your app name. One review per client app per tool per day counts. Only these fields are stored, never your prompts, arguments or address. We keep every review, good or bad, and never pay for ratings.

worked.description: true if the tool call you made worked.

missing.description: What you needed and did not get, in one or two sentences. No links.

tool.description: Optional: the tool name you are rating (default: the server as a whole).

client.description: Optional: your app or agent name.
